objection.quote: Conjecture: there is a finite set of primes S (the "core" primes that appear early and cover the sequence) such that L = prod(S) (or lcm of early terms), and eventually the sequence consists exactly of all integers > some point that are divisible by at least one prime from each of certain covering sets
objection.witness: MISSING: a proof, valid for all terms, that membership depends only on primes in a fixed finite set (e.g. primes <= a_1 or <= a_1^2) — i.e. that any term divisible by a large prime is dominated by a smaller integer with the same small-prime support which is itself a term (large-prime erasure). The quoted passage explicitly labels this a 'Conjecture' supported by computations on particular starting values, and gives no argument.
objection.load_bearing: Finiteness of the relevant prime set is exactly what makes L exist; the text's L = prod(S) is meaningless until S is proved finite and sufficient.
